findings.title: New abstract method order() breaks all external CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: The PR adds `int order();` as an abstract method to the public `CryptoProvider` interface in keycloak-common. Any third-party or downstream implementation of this interface (the interface is explicitly designed for pluggable crypto integrations, e.g. custom FIPS providers) will now fail to compile or throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when the new CryptoIntegration sorting calls order(). Making it a default method (e.g. `default int order() { return 100; }`) would preserve compatibility while still allowing the built-in providers to override it.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns an arbitrary JRE provider, not BouncyCastle
findings.body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the provider of the JVM default keystore (typically the SUN provider). Callers of CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getBouncyCastleProvider() reasonably expect a BouncyCastle(-like) provider and pass it to JCE getInstance(..., provider) calls for BC-specific algorithms; with this implementation they will get NoSuchAlgorithmException or silently use a provider that lacks the expected algorithms. If this provider is selected (it wins whenever no other CryptoProvider jar is present, which is exactly the standalone authz-client scenario), any code path touching getBouncyCastleProvider() misbehaves instead of failing clearly. Returning null or throwing UnsupportedOperationException like the other unsupported methods would be safer.

findings.title: readSequence() silently accepts indefinite-length encoding and returns incomplete data
findings.body: ASN1Decoder.readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (0x80), and readSequence() uses `while (length > 0)`, so an indefinite-length SEQUENCE is silently parsed as an empty sequence instead of being rejected. The caller in AuthzClientCryptoProvider.asn1derToConcatenatedRS then throws only a misleading 'Invalid sequence with size different to 2'. Since the decoder is only meant to handle DER (which forbids indefinite lengths), readSequence should throw an IOException when readLength() returns -1 to fail loudly on malformed input.

findings.title: Dead code: two ASN1Encoder results discarded in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: In concatenatedRSToASN1DER, lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances and call write(rBigInteger)/write(sBigInteger) on them, but the results are thrown away; the actual encoding is redone in the return statement with fresh encoders. This dead code is confusing and should be removed.

findings.title: Test uses a P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and only asserts round-trip
findings.body: ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates a single default-curve (P-256) EC key pair in the constructor and reuses it for testES384 and testES512, so the signatures being converted were produced by a curve that doesn't match those algorithms' real key sizes. Additionally the test only asserts that derToRS(rsToDer(x)) == x; it never verifies the produced DER against a Signature.verify() or a known-good JWS vector, so a systematically wrong encoding that round-trips would go undetected. Verifying the re-encoded DER with java.security.Signature (initialized with the matching curve key) would make the test meaningful.
